messages.content: Survey recent work on baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum. Use the hydrodynamics emulator tools to predict the Pk-ratio at z=0 for a couple of parameter points, explain the AGN feedback physics of suppression, and assess the impact on weak-lensing cosmology.

**Survey** — 52 tools on 5 servers, 7 read-only probes, 18 papers found.

Warning: none of my tools is a hydrodynamics or baryonic-emulator tool. I only had arXiv search, metadata lookup and web search, so I did not compute Pk-ratio values at z=0 for any parameter point. That step has to go to a role or tool that can run an emulator, such as BCemu, BACCO or the FLAMINGO Gaussian-process emulator. Some numbers below are general knowledge, not from returned abstracts, and need checking; the one returned figure is about 10 percent suppression at k=1 h/Mpc (2512.02954).

What the literature says: baryonic feedback lowers the total matter power spectrum relative to a dark-matter-only run. The effect is small near k of about 0.1 to 1 h/Mpc, reaches a minimum of roughly 10 to 30 percent around k of about 5 to 20 h/Mpc at z=0, and turns upward at higher k because stars cool and pile up in halo centres (van Daalen et al. 2011, 1104.1174; library of 92 simulations, 1906.00968). The main driver is AGN feedback in groups and clusters of about 1e13 to 1e14 Msun. It pushes gas out beyond the virial radius, lowering halo baryon fractions and making profiles shallower. So the suppression tracks the gas fraction in groups and clusters (2309.06479, 2309.02920, 2509.04552, 2511.10634). FLAMINGO finds that lower cluster gas fractions, collimated jets rather than thermal AGN feedback, and lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction all deepen the suppression. The suppression also gets stronger and moves to smaller scales as redshift falls, with only about 1 percent dependence on cosmology (2410.17109).

There is an open tension between data sets. FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS were calibrated to HSC-XXL X-ray gas fractions, which prefer about 5 +/- 4 percent suppression at k=1 h/Mpc. Joint eROSITA plus ACT kSZ data prefer 10 +/- 2 percent at k=1 h/Mpc, which is stronger feedback than the fiducial simulations (2512.02954). For weak lensing, unmodelled suppression pushes S8 low on small scales. Some authors argue that strong suppression could explain the S8 tension between lensing and Planck (2206.11794, 2305.09827). FLAMINGO finds that baryonic physics consistent with X-ray data cannot fully resolve it (2309.07959). DES Y3 small-scale shear has been used to constrain baryonic-correction-model parameters directly (2206.08591).

Quantities worth checking: Pk ratio at z=0 (hydro over dark-matter-only) for k from 0.1 to 10 h/Mpc, at a fiducial point and a strong-feedback point (for example FLAMINGO fiducial versus the fgas-8sigma or jet runs, or BCemu with log10 Mc of about 13.5 versus 14.5). These numbers have not been computed.; Depth and wavenumber of the suppression minimum at z=0; FLAMINGO says it moves to higher k as redshift decreases.; Suppression at k=1 h/Mpc compared with the 10 +/- 2 percent (eROSITA plus kSZ) and 5 +/- 4 percent (HSC-XXL) constraints in 2512.02954.; Relation between suppression and halo baryon fraction for groups and clusters of about 1e14 Msun.; Suppression of the cosmic shear signal (C_ell or xi_plus) for ell of about 1000 to 5000, and the S8 shift if baryons are ignored..

**Plan** — 4 lines of investigation:
1. Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict the matter power spectrum ratio P_hydro/P_DMO at z=0 for k from about 0.1 to 10 h/Mpc at two or three parameter points: fiducial, strong AGN feedback and weak AGN feedback. Report the depth and wavenumber of the suppression minimum and the suppression at k=1 h/Mpc. — This is the computation the task asks for directly. The survey brief notes that no Pk-ratio values have been computed yet. Single emulator evaluations run quickly on the local machine, so no facility run is needed.
2. Build a cited literature synthesis covering two topics: (a) the AGN feedback physics that causes baryonic suppression, and (b) its impact on weak-lensing cosmology, including the S8 bias and mitigation methods. Extract numerical benchmarks to compare against the emulator results. — The task asks for an explanation of the physics and an assessment of the weak-lensing impact. Published results are needed for both. The survey left some numbers flagged as general knowledge rather than sourced, and those need verified quotes.
3. Robustness and physics cross-checks with the emulator. Test sensitivity of the z=0 Pk-ratio to each feedback parameter separately and to cosmology. Check redshift evolution of the suppression minimum. Link suppression to the group and cluster gas fraction using the emulator's fGas observable. — This direction goes beyond the two-point comparison. It tests the literature claims that suppression tracks halo gas fraction, deepens and shifts to higher k as z decreases, and depends only weakly on cosmology (about 1 percent per 2410.17109), using the same emulator.
4. Cited literature synthesis of the impact of baryonic suppression on weak-lensing cosmology: the S8 bias if baryons are ignored, the suppression amplitude needed to reconcile shear with Planck, and mitigation methods. — Within its budget, d-02 cannot also cover the weak-lensing half of the task. No tool can compute a lensing quantity, so this part must rest entirely on verified quotes. (added by the critic)
Critic's view: revise — The HACC Pk-ratio output may not cover k=0.1 to 10 h/Mpc, and its redshifts may be a discrete list. After list_observables or describe_parameters, record the actual k range and report the minimum only if it lies inside that range. Do not extrapolate. If the curve has no turnover before k_max, state that the minimum is not resolved.; Robustness: at k=1 h/Mpc and at the minimum, compare the difference between the strong-feedback and weak-feedback curves with the emulator uncertainty band. State whether the variants can be distinguished.; Interpretation guard: HACC subgrid parameters are not the same as the FLAMINGO fgas or jet variants, nor the BCemu log10 Mc. Present the comparison with the 5 +/- 4 percent and 10 +/- 2 percent constraints (2512.02954) as a range-of-model check, not a calibration. Do not attribute any computed number to FLAMINGO, BCemu or BACCO, since none of those emulators is available..

**Wave 1** — now exploring, in parallel: Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict the matter power spectrum ratio P_hydro/P_DMO at z=0 for k from about 0.1 to 10 h/Mpc at two or three parameter points: fiducial, strong AGN feedback and weak AGN feedback. Report the depth and wavenumber of the suppression minimum and the suppression at k=1 h/Mpc.; Build a cited literature synthesis covering two topics: (a) the AGN feedback physics that causes baryonic suppression, and (b) its impact on weak-lensing cosmology, including the S8 bias and mitigation methods. Extract numerical benchmarks to compare against the emulator results.; Cited literature synthesis of the impact of baryonic suppression on weak-lensing cosmology: the S8 bias if baryons are ignored, the suppression amplitude needed to reconcile shear with Planck, and mitigation methods..

**Finding:** HACC emulator Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_grav) at z=0, cosmology fixed (omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8, kappa_w=3, M_seed=1.3). Fiducial (e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61): 0.99968 at k=0.101, 0.99197 at k=0.510, 0.97832+/-0.00096 at k=0.997 (2.2% suppression), 0.95104+/-0.00229 at k=2.00, 0.91968+/-0.00346 at k=3.01, 0.8979 at k=3.71 h/Mpc. Strong AGN (e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2): 0.99962, 0.99062, 0.97506+/-0.00175 (2.5%), 0.94463+/-0.00405, 0.91207+/-0.00596, 0.8904 at the same k. Suppression still deepens at k=3.7 h/Mpc in both runs, so the minimum lies above k=3.7. At k=1 h/Mpc both runs are within 1 sigma of HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) and well below eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%, 2512.02954), which is excluded at more than 3.5 sigma. Driving all three AGN/kinetic parameters to their upper limits changes the k=1 suppression by only about 0.3 percentage points.

**Finding:** The HACC Pk-ratio at z=0 for the weak-AGN point (kappa_w=3, e_w=0.2, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) shows no suppression. Instead it shows an enhancement: 1.00009 at k=0.101, 1.00096 at k=0.510 and 1.0023+/-0.0025 at k=0.997 h/Mpc. The ratio peaks at about 1.0097+/-0.0072 near k of about 2.4 h/Mpc and falls back to 1.0012+/-0.0105 at k=3.71 h/Mpc. Across the full design range of the AGN and kinetic parameters, the k=1 h/Mpc suppression spans only about -0.2% to +2.5%. The emulator is therefore consistent with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) at the strong end but cannot reach eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%). At k=1 the emulator 1-sigma (0.1-0.25%) is comparable to the fiducial-versus-strong difference (0.33%) but smaller than the weak-versus-fiducial difference (2.4%).

**Finding:** Literature synthesis from full texts that were read: (1) Mechanism: energy from active galactic nuclei (AGN) moves gas relative to the dark matter. This suppresses the nonlinear matter power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954). Below about 10 Mpc, AGN redistribute baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920). In FLAMINGO, lower group and cluster gas fractions, collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction all strengthen the response. As z falls, the response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The cosmology dependence is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc (2410.17109). (2) Benchmarks: suppression at k=1 h/Mpc is 10+/-2 percent from eROSITA plus kSZ and 5+/-4 percent from HSC-XXL, over 13<log10 M500/(Msun/h)<14 and 0<z<1 (2512.02954). Cluster baryon-correction-model priors give 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc, with less than 1 percent impact at k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility (2309.02920). (3) Weak lensing: Amon and Efstathiou find that KiDS-1000 (S8 = 0.759 +0.024/-0.021) can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794). FLAMINGO finds baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension (2309.07959). Mitigation is to calibrate feedback with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

**Finding:** Literature (quoted, cited): Amon & Efstathiou (2206.11794) find KiDS-1000 xi_pm is consistent with Planck LCDM only if non-linear power is suppressed with A_mod ~ 0.69, extending to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, outside the BAHAMAS range; FLAMINGO (2309.07959) finds baryonic effects across its feedback variants are not large enough to remove the S8 tension; Siegel et al. (2512.02954) find eROSITA+kSZ prefer 10+/-2% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc (HSC-XXL 5+/-4%), only BAHAMAS 8.0 and FLAMINGO fgas-8sigma agree, simulations differ by >10% at k=1 h/Mpc, and in an LSST-Y1 mock, ignoring baryons significantly biases S8, an uninformed baryonification model costs 2x in precision, and the kSZ+eROSITA prior recovers half of that lost precision.

**Finding:** This is a qualitative comparison only, and the d-01 HACC emulator values were not on the board when it was posted. Any emulator suppression at k=1 h/Mpc should be read against these benchmarks: about 5% (HSC-XXL, consistent with fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS), 10+/-2% (eROSITA+kSZ, strong feedback), and the much stronger, larger-scale suppression (A_mod ~ 0.69, reaching k~0.2 h/Mpc) that Amon & Efstathiou need to reconcile KiDS with Planck. A suppression of 10% or less at k=1 h/Mpc would, per FLAMINGO 2309.07959, not by itself remove the S8 tension.

**Completed — Cited literature synthesis of the impact of baryonic suppression on weak-lensing cosmology: the S8 bias if baryons are ignored, the suppression amplitude needed to reconcile shear with Planck, and mitigation methods..** Three papers were read and cited with verbatim quotes in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/references.bib.

(1) Amon & Efstathiou (2206.11794): KiDS-1000 cosmic shear is consistent with Planck LCDM if non-linear power is suppressed with A_mod ~ 0.69. The suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, which is well outside the BAHAMAS range.

(2) FLAMINGO (2309.07959): across its range of feedback variants, baryonic effects are not large enough to remove the S8 tension; the paper says 'it is unlikely that baryon physics is driving this modification'.

(3) Siegel et al. (2512.02954): joint eROSITA and kSZ data give 10+/-2% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc, while HSC-XXL gives 5+/-4%. Only the strong-feedback runs BAHAMAS 8.0 and FLAMINGO fgas-8sigma agree with the eROSITA and kSZ result, and the simulations differ from each other by more than 10% at k=1 h/Mpc. Mitigation, from their LSST Y1-like mock (Fig. 6 of that paper): with no baryon model, S8 is significantly biased. An uninformed baryonification model removes the bias but halves the precision. A prior calibrated on kSZ and eROSITA recovers half of the lost precision. The paper reports this bias only graphically and gives no numerical S8 shift.

Findings f-004 (the literature numbers) and f-005 (qualitative comparison framework) are posted. The comparison with d-01 is only a framework so far, because the d-01 emulator values at k=1 h/Mpc were not on the board when I posted. No lensing quantity was computed. 2305.09827, 2206.08591 and 2410.12500 were not read.

**Blocked — Build a cited literature synthesis covering two topics: (a) the AGN feedback physics that causes baryonic suppression, and (b) its impact on weak-lensing cosmology, including the S8 bias and mitigation methods. Extract numerical benchmarks to compare against the emulator results..** (The tool budget ran out before the remaining success criteria were met. Only 3 of the required 5 papers were cited; 2512.02954 and 2309.02920 were read but not cited. No figure was extracted from 2410.17109, and the papers were not read past their abstracts and introductions. As a result, three numbers are still unsourced: the depth and k of FLAMINGO's z=0 minimum, the ell range affected in lensing, and the size of the S8 shift. These remaining items are logged as question q-05.) This direction is only partly done. The literature synthesis is posted as finding f-003 and rests on the abstracts and introductions of five full texts. These are saved under /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ as 2410.17109.txt, 2512.02954.txt, 2309.07959.txt, 2206.11794.txt and 2309.02920.txt.

Mechanism, from those texts:
- Energy injected by AGN moves gas relative to the dark matter and suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954).
- Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920).
- In FLAMINGO (2410.17109), the response is stronger for lower group and cluster gas fractions, for collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and for lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- As redshift falls, the FLAMINGO response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The dependence on cosmology is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc. Its emulator is accurate to better than 1 percent up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.

Benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc:
- eROSITA plus kSZ: 10 +/- 2 percent; HSC-XXL: 5 +/- 4 percent. Both are for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (2512.02954).
- Cluster-based baryon-correction priors (2309.02920): 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc. The effect is below 1 percent for k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility.

Weak lensing:
- KiDS-1000 shear gives S8 = 0.759 (+0.024/-0.021). This can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794).
- FLAMINGO concludes that baryon physics is unlikely to be driving the S8 tension (2309.07959).
- The mitigation route demonstrated for LSST Y1 is to calibrate feedback models with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

Citations: 2410.17109, 2309.07959 and 2206.11794 were cited with verbatim quotes into references.bib in the run directory.

**Completed — Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict the matter power spectrum ratio P_hydro/P_DMO at z=0 for k from about 0.1 to 10 h/Mpc at two or three parameter points: fiducial, strong AGN feedback and weak AGN feedback. Report the depth and wavenumber of the suppression minimum and the suppression at k=1 h/Mpc..** I ran three HACC Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_grav) predictions at z=0 with cosmology held fixed (omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8, kappa_w=3, M_seed=1.3). Two success criteria are not fully met: values at k=5-10 h/Mpc and the location and depth of the suppression minimum were not extracted. The text reader cuts each 799-bin CSV off near k=3.7 h/Mpc, and load_table_data rejects the CSV header row (posted as q-06). The fiducial point is the centre of the parameter ranges, not a calibrated fiducial.

Parameter points:
- fiducial_z0: e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61
- strongAGN_z0: e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2
- weakAGN_z0: e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02

Ratio at k=0.10 / 0.51 / 1.00 / 2.00 / 3.0 / 3.71 h/Mpc:
- Fiducial: 0.99968 / 0.99197 / 0.97832+/-0.00096 / 0.95104+/-0.00229 / 0.91968 / 0.8979
- Strong: 0.99962 / 0.99062 / 0.97506+/-0.00175 / 0.94463+/-0.00405 / 0.91207 / 0.8904
- Weak: 1.00009 / 1.00096 / 1.0023+/-0.0025 / 1.0089 / 1.0074 / 1.0012+/-0.0105. This is an enhancement, peaking at about 1.0097 near k=2.4 h/Mpc.

For the fiducial and strong points the suppression is still deepening at k=3.7 h/Mpc, so their minimum lies above k=3.7 h/Mpc.

Comparison at k=1 h/Mpc: suppression is 2.2% (fiducial), 2.5% (strong) and -0.2% (weak). All three agree with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) within about 1.4 sigma. None reaches eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%, 2512.02954); the strong point falls short by about 3.7 sigma. Pushing e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their upper limits changes the k=1 suppression by only about 0.3 percentage points relative to the fiducial. The emulator 1-sigma at k=1 (0.1-0.25%) is comparable to that fiducial-to-strong difference but well below the weak-to-fiducial difference (2.4%).

Findings f-001 and f-002 posted; open question q-06 posted.

**Critic, wave 1** — continue: 3 findings stand up to the evidence, 2 questioned ('The HACC Pk-ratio at z=0 for the weak-AGN point (kappa_w=3, e_w=0.2, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.1': The claim that the k=1 h/Mpc suppression 'across the full design range of the AGN and kinetic parameters' spans only about -0.2% to +2.5% is not supported. Only three corner-like points were run. kappa_w (fixed at 3), M_seed and cosmology were never varied, and the parameter bounds were not shown in any cited evidence (no describe_parameters output). The quoted CSV excerpts (tc-...-49, -31, -37) also stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The peak of 1.0097 near k=2.4 and the k=1 and k=3.71 values are not visible in the evidence; only the k=0.101 value (1.00009) can be checked. The weak-point measurements may be right, but the design-range generalisation must be removed or backed by a parameter scan.; 'Literature synthesis from full texts that were read: (1) Mechanism: energy from active gal': Every evidence excerpt is the title and author header (chars 0-4000) of a paper. None contains the specific numbers claimed: 10+/-2 and 5+/-4 percent, 0.042 and 0.184 at k=1 and 3 h/Mpc, k<0.37 at 97.5 percent, S8=0.759, or about 1 percent cosmology dependence. 2309.02920 was never cited through the cite tool, so no verbatim quote is stored for its numbers. The numbers are plausible and partly corroborated by f-004 for 2512.02954, but this finding's own evidence does not contain them.).

Issues: The quoted CSV excerpts stop at k=0.117 h/Mpc. The values at k=0.51, 1, 2, 3 and 3.71 are not visible in the cited evidence; only the k=0.101 values (0.99968 fiducial, 0.99962 strong) can be checked. The k=1 values are the key numbers of the task and should be re-extracted with a working reader and quoted directly (q-06). The finding is accepted on the summary's account, but this is a weak point.; Wording of the comparison. The phrase 'eROSITA+kSZ ... excluded at more than 3.5 sigma' reverses the logic. The emulator cannot exclude a measurement. The correct statement is that the sampled HACC points fall short of the eROSITA+kSZ value by about 3.7 sigma (observational error only). The comparison also mixes a fixed HACC cosmology (omega_m=0.14, probably omega_m h^2) with observational constraints derived under a different cosmology and halo-mass weighting. It should be framed as a range-of-model check, as critique c-01 required.; There is a physics discrepancy no one has noted. At k=3 h/Mpc the HACC fiducial and strong points give about 8-9 percent suppression, while the cluster-calibrated prior of 2309.02920 gives 18.4 percent (+2.6/-3.1). At k=1 the emulator gives 2.2-2.5 percent against 4.2 percent there and 5-10 percent from 2512.02954. In addition, the weak-AGN point shows a net enhancement, and the strong AGN parameters barely matter (0.3 percentage points). Together these suggest that the parameters held fixed (kappa_w, M_seed), or the parameter interpretation itself, control most of the suppression. This must be resolved before any conclusion about feedback strength..

**Next steps after wave 1** — This is the final wave, with 15 tool calls. d-03 was never run, but its scope (per-parameter scans, cosmology, redshift, fGas) is too broad for the remaining budget. The critic's high-severity issue also shows that kappa_w and M_seed, not the AGN parameters already varied, are the likely controls. d-03 is therefore closed and replaced by a narrowed child: describe_parameters, kappa_w at both bounds, M_seed at one bound, extraction of the CSVs past k=3.7, and one plot, about 7 calls. d-02 was blocked by budget, and its remaining sourcing items (2309.02920 quotes, the FLAMINGO minimum, the comparison table replacing the stale f-005) move to a focused literature cross-check of about 4-5 calls that uses texts already downloaded. The unaddressed weak-lensing requirement gets a small direction of about 3 calls sourcing the DES Y3 A_mod and a second mitigation method, and flags a shear forecast as future work. The task does not require facility runs, so all compute stays local. The steps also carry the critic's wording fixes for f-001, f-002 and f-004.

New lines of investigation: Find out which HACC emulator parameters control the z=0 Pk-ratio suppression, and resolve the curve beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc. This is a budget-limited replacement for d-03.; Close the literature sourcing gaps and cross-check the HACC suppression amplitude against published calibrated values at k=1 and k=3 h/Mpc.; Source the cosmic-shear impact of baryonic suppression: the affected ell or theta range, the DES Y3 A_mod, and a second mitigation method..

**Wave 2** — now exploring, in parallel: Find out which HACC emulator parameters control the z=0 Pk-ratio suppression, and resolve the curve beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc. This is a budget-limited replacement for d-03.; Close the literature sourcing gaps and cross-check the HACC suppression amplitude against published calibrated values at k=1 and k=3 h/Mpc.; Source the cosmic-shear impact of baryonic suppression: the affected ell or theta range, the DES Y3 A_mod, and a second mitigation method..

**Finding:** Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) find that to reconcile DES Y3 cosmic shear with Planck LCDM, the non-linear suppression needed is weaker than the KiDS-1000 value (A_mod ~ 0.69). It is still more extreme than recent hydrodynamic simulations predict, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. The DES Y3 A_mod value itself was not in the text I read (abstract and conclusions), so it remains unsourced.

**Finding:** Second mitigation method (Maraio, Hall & Taylor, 2410.12500): a theoretical-error covariance built into the matter power spectrum, used in place of binary ell scale cuts. For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models can introduce significant bias. The theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in variance, and it removes the need to choose an ell_max for each bin. This places the baryon-sensitive shear range up to ell ~ 5000.

**Finding:** Approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator gives about 0.8-0.9% suppression at k=0.5 h/Mpc, about 0.03-0.04% at k=0.1 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc (f-001, f-002). This is far below the A_mod-type suppression that Amon-Efstathiou and Preston et al. require. That suppression scales the whole non-linear part of P(k) (A_mod ~ 0.69 for KiDS, weaker but still beyond simulations for DES) and reaches down to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Within its design range, the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A projected C_ell or xi_+ forecast is future work, since no tool computes it.

**Blocked — Source the cosmic-shear impact of baryonic suppression: the affected ell or theta range, the DES Y3 A_mod, and a second mitigation method..** (The tool budget ran out before the DES Y3 A_mod number could be read from the body of 2305.09827 and before the cite calls. Both are logged as q-07.) Partly done. Three success criteria are not met: (1) the DES Y3 A_mod number was not found; (2) nothing was run through cite, so 2305.09827 and 2410.12500 are not in references.bib; (3) no theta range was sourced. What was established, from full texts saved in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ (2305.09827.txt, 2410.12500.txt): (a) Finding f-006. For DES Y3, Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) use the model P_m = P_L + A_mod(P_NL - P_L). They find the suppression needed to resolve the S8 tension 'is not as strong as inferred using KiDS data' (KiDS A_mod ~ 0.69) 'but is still more extreme than predictions from recent numerical simulations'. It must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. I quoted this from the abstract but did not read the numerical DES A_mod. (b) Finding f-007. As a second mitigation method, Maraio, Hall & Taylor (2410.12500) put a theoretical-error covariance into the matter power spectrum in place of ell scale cuts. With ell_max = 5000 for a Euclid-like survey, it reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with a modest increase in variance. The first mitigation method, multi-wavelength calibration from 2512.02954, is already in f-004. The only ell range sourced is that the baryon-sensitive shear goes up to ell ~ 5000. (c) Finding f-008, an approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator suppression is about 0.8-0.9% at k=0.5 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc. This is far below the A_mod-level suppression reaching k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc, so within its design range the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A C_ell or xi_+ lensing forecast is flagged as future work, which answers q-03.

**Finding:** Sourced with verbatim quotes in references.bib (key arxiv230902920): Grandis et al. 2309.02920 find a baryonic suppression of the matter power of 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc in their fiducial baryon-correction model. This direction is only partly done. The literature synthesis is posted as finding f-003 and rests on the abstracts and introductions of five full texts. These are saved under /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261017_143153/ as 2410.17109.txt, 2512.02954.txt, 2309.07959.txt, 2206.11794.txt and 2309.02920.txt.

Mechanism, from those texts:
- Energy injected by AGN moves gas relative to the dark matter and suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent compared with dark-matter-only runs (2512.02954).
- Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward, while on smaller scales star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (2309.02920).
- In FLAMINGO (2410.17109), the response is stronger for lower group and cluster gas fractions, for collimated jets instead of thermal winds, and for lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- As redshift falls, the FLAMINGO response grows and its minimum moves to smaller scales. The dependence on cosmology is about 1 percent at k<10 h/Mpc. Its emulator is accurate to better than 1 percent up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.

Benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc:
- eROSITA plus kSZ: 10 +/- 2 percent; HSC-XXL: 5 +/- 4 percent. Both are for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (2512.02954).
- Cluster-based baryon-correction priors (2309.02920): 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k=1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k=3 h/Mpc. The effect is below 1 percent for k<0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5 percent credibility.

Weak lensing:
- KiDS-1000 shear gives S8 = 0.759 (+0.024/-0.021). This can be reconciled with Planck LCDM if nonlinear power is suppressed more strongly than simulations predict (2206.11794).
- FLAMINGO concludes that baryon physics is unlikely to be driving the S8 tension (2309.07959).
- The mitigation route demonstrated for LSST Y1 is to calibrate feedback models with multi-wavelength gas observables (2512.02954).

Citations: 2410.17109, 2309.07959 and 2206.11794 were cited with verbatim quotes into references.bib in the run directory.

messages.report:
# Baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum: HACC emulator predictions at z=0 and a literature assessment of AGN feedback and weak-lensing impact

## Abstract

We used the HACC hydrodynamics emulator to predict the z=0 ratio P_hydro/P_grav at six parameter points, holding cosmology fixed at omega_m=0.14 and sigma_8=0.8.

- **Suppression at k=1 h/Mpc.** It runs from an enhancement of 0.2% at the weakest AGN point to 2.9% suppression at the lowest wind coupling (kappa_w=2).
- **Suppression at k=3 h/Mpc.** The largest sampled value is 10.9%.
- **Comparison with observations.** Every sampled point is consistent with the HSC-XXL gas-fraction constraint of 5+/-4% at k=1. All of them fall well short of the eROSITA+kSZ preference of 10+/-2%. At k=3 they also fall short of the cluster-calibrated 18.4% from arXiv:2309.02920.
- **Unresolved curve shape.** The emulator curves are still deepening at k≈3.7 h/Mpc, the furthest point we could read. The suppression minimum and the high-k upturn are therefore not resolved.

From the literature, AGN feedback in groups and clusters ejects gas and drives the suppression. Lower cluster gas fractions and jet-mode feedback strengthen it. For weak lensing, reconciling KiDS or DES shear with Planck through baryons alone requires suppression stronger and reaching larger scales than current simulations predict. FLAMINGO concludes that baryons are unlikely to drive the S8 tension.

We computed no lensing observable.

## Background

The effect of galaxy formation on the total matter power spectrum was established with the OWLS simulations (arXiv:1104.1174). A library of 92 simulation power spectra provides benchmark ratios (arXiv:1906.00968). The commonly quoted shape is a 10–30% minimum at k≈5–20 h/Mpc followed by a high-k upturn. That shape was flagged in the survey as general knowledge and was not sourced from these papers during the run.

Within the texts that were read, the mechanism is as follows:

- **Gas redistribution.** Energy injected by AGN redistributes gas relative to the dark matter. This suppresses small-scale power by tens of percent relative to dark-matter-only runs (arXiv:2512.02954).
- **Outward and inward baryon motion.** Below about 10 Mpc, AGN push baryons outward. On smaller scales, star formation concentrates baryons in halo centres (arXiv:2309.02920).
- **What strengthens the response in FLAMINGO** (arXiv:2410.17109):
  - lower gas fractions in groups and clusters;
  - collimated jets in place of thermal AGN feedback;
  - lower stellar mass at fixed gas fraction.
- **Redshift dependence in FLAMINGO.** The response grows as redshift falls.
  - The fiducial minimum moves from k=6 h/Mpc at z=2 to k=10 h/Mpc at z=0.
  - The departure from unity begins at k≈1 h/Mpc at z=2 and at k≈0.1 h/Mpc at z=0.
- **Gas-fraction variants in FLAMINGO.** Thermal-AGN variants spanning fgas −10σ to +4σ keep the z=0 minimum at k=8–10 h/Mpc. These variants mainly change the amplitude of the response.
  - The response saturates below fgas−8σ, which is an emulator extrapolation.
  - The jet model has a similar k-range and minimum position.
- **Cosmology dependence and accuracy in FLAMINGO.** The cosmology dependence is about 1% at k<10 h/Mpc, and the emulator is accurate to better than 1% up to k=10 h/Mpc and z=3.
- **Depth of the FLAMINGO z=0 minimum.** The text states no number. It is shown only graphically, in Figs. 2, 5 and 6 of that paper.

Observational benchmarks at k=1 h/Mpc, for haloes with 13<log10 M500<14 at 0<z<1 (arXiv:2512.02954):

| Constraint | Suppression at k=1 h/Mpc | Agreement with simulations |
|---|---|---|
| eROSITA+kSZ | 10+/-2% | Only the strong-feedback runs BAHAMAS 8.0 and FLAMINGO fgas−8σ agree |
| HSC-XXL | 5+/-4% | — |

The same paper notes that the simulations differ from each other by more than 10% at k=1 h/Mpc.

Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) derive cluster-based baryon-correction results:

| Model | Suppression at k=1 h/Mpc | Suppression at k=3 h/Mpc |
|---|---|---|
| Fiducial | 0.042 (+0.012/−0.014) | 0.184 (+0.026/−0.031) |
| Alternative | 0.049 | 0.179 |

At 97.5% credibility they find an impact below 1% for k<0.37 h/Mpc. They state that some hydrodynamical simulations have feedback that is either too strong or too weak.

For weak lensing, the relevant results are:

- **KiDS-1000.** Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) show that KiDS-1000 shear, with S8 = 0.759 (+0.024/−0.021), can be reconciled with Planck ΛCDM if the non-linear power is suppressed with A_mod≈0.69. This is a sufficient route, not shown to be the only one. The suppression must extend to k≈0.2 h/Mpc, outside the BAHAMAS range.
- **DES Y3.** Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) find that DES Y3 requires a weaker suppression than KiDS. It is still more extreme than recent hydrodynamic simulations predict. They note that underestimating baryonic effects is not the only possible interpretation.
- **FLAMINGO.** FLAMINGO (arXiv:2309.07959) finds that "it is unlikely that baryon physics is driving this modification."
- **Mitigation by gas calibration.** Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) use an LSST-Y1-like mock.
  - Ignoring baryons biases S8 significantly.
  - An uninformed baryonification model removes the bias but roughly doubles the S8 uncertainty.
  - A kSZ+eROSITA-calibrated prior recovers about half of the lost precision.
  - The bias is shown only graphically.
- **Mitigation by theoretical-error covariance.** Maraio, Hall & Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500) replace scale cuts with a theoretical-error covariance in P(k). For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max=5000, this reduces the bias in Ω_m and S8 to acceptable levels with a modest increase in variance. This statement rests on that paper's abstract and was not independently verified by the critic.

Other relevant tools named in the survey are BCemu (arXiv:2108.08863), the baryonic correction model (arXiv:1810.08629) and the analytic model of arXiv:2504.15633. None of these was available to run.

## Results

### HACC emulator: fiducial, strong and weak AGN points

The HACC Pk-ratio emulator has a 7-parameter design built from 110 simulations in 400 Mpc/h boxes. Its parameters and ranges are:

| Parameter | Meaning | Range |
|---|---|---|
| kappa_w | AGN wind coupling | [2, 4] |
| e_w | AGN energy efficiency | [0.2, 1] |
| M_seed | Black-hole seed mass, in 10^6 Msun | [0.6, 2] |
| v_kin | Kinetic feedback velocity, in 10^4 km/s | [0.1, 1.2] |
| eps_kin | Kinetic efficiency, in units of 10 | [0.02, 1.2] |
| omega_m | Ω_m h² | [0.12, 0.155] |
| sigma_8 | — | [0.7, 0.9] |

The reference spectrum is the emulator's P_grav, not a matched dark-matter-only run.

All runs are at z=0 with omega_m=0.14 and sigma_8=0.8. The "fiducial" point is the centre of the parameter ranges, not a calibrated model. The three points are:

- **Fiducial:** e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61.
- **Strong:** e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2.
- **Weak:** e_w=0.2, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02.

All three use kappa_w=3 and M_seed=1.3.

| k [h/Mpc] | Fiducial | Strong | Weak |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 0.99968 | 0.99962 | 1.00009 |
| 0.51 | 0.99197 | 0.99062 | 1.00096 |
| 1.00 | 0.97832+/-0.00096 | 0.97506+/-0.00175 | 1.0023+/-0.0025 |
| 2.00 | 0.95104+/-0.00229 | 0.94463+/-0.00405 | 1.0089 |
| 3.0 | 0.91968+/-0.00346 | 0.91207+/-0.00596 | 1.0074 |
| 3.71 | 0.8979 | 0.8904 | 1.0012+/-0.0105 |

Expressed as suppression at k=1 h/Mpc, the values are 2.2% (fiducial), 2.5% (strong) and −0.2% (weak). The negative value means the weak point is enhanced.

The weak point shows no suppression anywhere in the readable range. Its ratio peaks at about 1.0097+/-0.0072 near k≈2.4 h/Mpc. We do not have a sourced physical explanation for this enhancement in the emulator.

Moving e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their upper bounds changes the k=1 suppression by only about 0.3 percentage points relative to the fiducial. That shift is comparable to the emulator 1σ at k=1, which is 0.1–0.25%. The weak-to-fiducial difference of 2.4 pp is well resolved.

The suppression in the fiducial and strong runs is still deepening at k=3.71 h/Mpc. Their minimum therefore lies at higher k and was not measured.

Figure 8 overlays the three z=0 ratio curves (fiducial, strong, weak) produced by the emulator plotting tool:

[[FIGURE 8]]

Figure 9 shows the fiducial prediction with its emulator uncertainty band:

[[FIGURE 9]]

Warning: the board's quoted CSV excerpts stop near k≈0.12 h/Mpc. Every value at k≥0.5 h/Mpc is therefore taken from the run summaries and could not be checked against the quoted tool output.

The original statement that the full AGN design range spans only −0.2% to +2.5% at k=1 was contested. It is contradicted by the kappa_w=2 run below. That statement is superseded by the six-point summary given later in this section.

### One-at-a-time sensitivity: kappa_w and M_seed

Each run below varies one parameter and keeps all others at the fiducial values. Suppression is 1−P_hydro/P_grav, with the emulator 1σ in brackets.

| Run | k=0.997 | k=3.007 | k=3.714 h/Mpc |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fiducial | 2.17% (0.10%) | 8.03% (0.35%) | 10.2% |
| kappa_w=2 | 2.92% (0.15%) | 10.93% (0.54%) | 13.66% (0.64%) |
| kappa_w=4 | 1.31% (0.13%) | 4.95% (0.46%) | 6.60% (0.54%) |
| M_seed=2.0 | 2.42% (0.14%) | 9.03% (0.49%) | 11.40% (0.57%) |

Lower wind coupling kappa_w strengthens the suppression.

Ranking the shifts from the fiducial gives the following.

- **At k=1:** the joint lowering of e_w, v_kin and eps_kin (−2.4 pp) is the largest. It is followed by kappa_w across its range (1.6 pp spread: +0.75 pp at kappa_w=2, −0.86 pp at kappa_w=4). Next is the joint raising of e_w, v_kin and eps_kin (+0.33 pp), and last is M_seed from 1.3 to 2.0 (+0.25 pp).
- **At k=3:** the joint lowering of e_w, v_kin and eps_kin (about −8.8 pp) is again the largest shift sampled. It is followed by kappa_w (5.98 pp spread; +2.9 pp at kappa_w=2), then M_seed (+1.0 pp), then the joint raising (+0.76 pp).

Of the parameters varied singly, kappa_w has the largest one-at-a-time effect. However, it is not the largest shift sampled, because the joint move of the three AGN energy and kinetic parameters toward their lower bounds is larger.

At k=3 every shift exceeds the emulator 1σ of 0.35–0.54%. At k=1 the M_seed shift and the joint-raising shift are only about 2σ.

e_w, v_kin and eps_kin were only ever moved together, so their individual sensitivities are unknown. omega_m and sigma_8 were never varied. As a result, the roughly 1% cosmology independence reported by FLAMINGO has not been checked for HACC.

For the kappa_w and M_seed runs, no values at k=0.1 or 0.5 h/Mpc are on the board. For the fiducial and strong points only, the large-scale suppression is about 0.03–0.04% at k=0.1 h/Mpc and about 0.8–0.9% at k=0.5 h/Mpc. The weak point is slightly enhanced at these k.

No comparison plot was produced for these runs.

### Comparison with observational and calibrated benchmarks

This is a range-of-model check, not a calibration. The cosmology and halo-mass weighting differ between HACC and the observational analyses, and HACC parameters do not map onto FLAMINGO fgas, FLAMINGO jet or BCemu parameters.

**At k=1 h/Mpc.** Across the six sampled points (fiducial, strong, weak, kappa_w=2, kappa_w=4, M_seed=2), the suppression spans −0.2% to 2.9%. None reaches 5% or 10%. The most suppressed point, kappa_w=2 at 2.92+/-0.15%:

- is about 0.5σ from HSC-XXL;
- falls short of eROSITA+kSZ by about 3.5σ, using the observational error only;
- relative to Grandis et al., the fiducial and strong points sit about 1.2–1.4σ below their 4.2%.

**At k=3 h/Mpc.** The fiducial and strong HACC points give 8.0% and 8.8%. These are a factor of about 2.1–2.3 below the 18.4% of arXiv:2309.02920, or about 3.1–3.4σ against that paper's lower error bar. The largest sampled value, 10.9+/-0.5% at kappa_w=2, is still about 2.4σ low.

This k=3 gap is unexplained, and the critic contested the comparison. Possible contributors are:

- HACC's minimum lies beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc, while FLAMINGO's lies at 8–10 h/Mpc, so the curve shapes may differ.
- The cosmologies and halo-mass ranges differ. arXiv:2309.02920 is calibrated on haloes above about 3e13 Msun.
- HACC uses P_grav as its reference spectrum.
- Combined extremes were not sampled, for example kappa_w=2 together with high e_w, v_kin, eps_kin and M_seed.

### Weak-lensing implications

No C_ell, xi_+ or S8 shift was computed, because no tool provides them. All lensing statements in this report come from the literature.

The A_mod-type suppression required by Amon & Efstathiou and Preston et al. scales the whole non-linear part of P(k), with A_mod≈0.69 for KiDS. It reaches down to k≈0.2 h/Mpc. The HACC fiducial and strong points suppress P(k) by less than 1% at k≤0.5 h/Mpc and by at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc.

Within the sampled range, the emulator is far from the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. This comparison is approximate and was contested by the critic as a rough mapping between different parameterisations.

FLAMINGO likewise reports that the Amon–Efstathiou response lies outside the reach of the FLAMINGO emulator (arXiv:2410.17109). Both of its fgas−8σ models, thermal and jet, fall inside the Bigwood et al. 2024 ranges, with or without kSZ.

The only sourced multipole range is that the baryon-sensitive shear extends to ell≈5000 (arXiv:2410.12500). The DES Y3 numerical A_mod was not read.

## Discussion

The emulator results agree qualitatively with the literature on two points:

- Suppression grows with k through the readable range.
- Suppression is weak on linear scales, below 1% at k<0.5 h/Mpc for the suppressed points. This is consistent with the <1% bound at k<0.37 h/Mpc from arXiv:2309.02920.

Quantitatively, the sampled HACC models are mild-feedback models. At k=1 they sit at the low end of the HSC-XXL range. They cannot reproduce the strong feedback preferred by eROSITA+kSZ (arXiv:2512.02954) or the k=3 cluster-calibrated amplitude (arXiv:2309.02920).

The weak-AGN corner even shows a net enhancement of about 1% near k≈2.4 h/Mpc. The sensitivity scan suggests that the amplitude is controlled more by kappa_w and by moving the energy and kinetic parameters toward their lower bounds than by raising them. Raising e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their maximum adds only 0.3–0.8 pp. This saturation is reminiscent of FLAMINGO's reported saturation below fgas−8σ. However, the two parameterisations are not comparable, and this resemblance is not a demonstrated link.

There is an unresolved tension at k=3 that cannot be settled without the curve beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc. If HACC's minimum sits at k≈8–10 h/Mpc like FLAMINGO's, the k=3 deficit reflects a genuinely weaker amplitude. If the shape differs, the comparison at a single k is misleading.

For weak lensing, the evidence assembled supports the FLAMINGO conclusion. Feedback consistent with X-ray gas fractions is not strong enough, nor large-scale enough, to remove the S8 tension. The KiDS and DES A_mod solutions require suppression extending to k≈0.2 h/Mpc, which is well beyond any of our sampled emulator points. The eROSITA+kSZ results favour stronger feedback than the fiducial simulations, which reopens part of this question. Even so, that paper's mitigation analysis treats baryons as a nuisance to calibrate, not as a resolution of the tension.

Dead ends:

- **Reading the CSVs beyond k≈3.73 h/Mpc.** The plain-text reader has no offset parameter and truncates each 799-bin CSV near k≈3.73 h/Mpc. The table loader rejects the header row, and no file-writing tool was available to make a header-free copy. As a result, values at k=5 and 10 h/Mpc, the minimum and any upturn were never extracted.
- **Running other baryonic emulators.** No BCemu, BACCO or FLAMINGO emulator was available. Every computed number is from HACC.

## Limitations

- **Truncated k range.** The k range effectively stops at 3.7 h/Mpc in our readout. The depth and position of the suppression minimum, which is a central quantity in the task, are not delivered. Whether the emulator itself reaches 10 h/Mpc is also not established.
- **Unverified mid- and high-k values.** The quoted evidence for every CSV ends near k≈0.12 h/Mpc. Values at k≥0.5 h/Mpc rest on run summaries.
- **Limited sampling.** Only six points were sampled, all at z=0 and at a single cosmology. There is no redshift scan, which matters because the lensing-weighted redshift is about 0.3–0.5. There is no cosmology variation, no fGas link and no combined-extreme points.
- **Missing literature numbers.** The FLAMINGO z=0 minimum depth and the DES Y3 A_mod are unsourced. arXiv:2305.09827 and arXiv:2410.12500 were not added to the bibliography. The 1104.1174 claims about the minimum and upturn were never verified.
- **No lensing calculation.** No projected lensing calculation was possible.
- **Budget.** The two-wave budget was exhausted. The planned robustness and cosmology cross-checks were replaced by the limited sensitivity scan reported above.

arXiv ID: 2410.17109
Title: The FLAMINGO project: Baryon effects on the matter power spectrum
Authors: Matthieu Schaller, Joop Schaye, Roi Kugel, Jeger C. Broxterman, Marcel P. van Daalen
Year: 2024
Abstract: The effect of baryon physics associated with galaxy formation onto the large-scale matter distribution of the Universe is a key uncertainty in the theoretical modelling required for the interpretation of Stage IV surveys. We use the FLAMINGO simulations to study the baryon response due to galaxy formation of the total matter power spectrum. We find that it is only well converged for simulation volumes in excess of $200^3$ Mpc$^3$. We report results for simulations of varying feedback intensity, which either match the X-ray inferred gas fractions in clusters and the $z=0$ stellar mass function, or shifted versions of the data, as well as for different implementations of AGN feedback. We package our results in the form of a Gaussian process emulator which can rapidly reproduce all the simulations' predictions to better than one per cent up to the comoving wavenumber $k = 10~h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and up to $z=3$ for all the feedback models present in the FLAMINGO suite. We find that the response becomes stronger, the range of scales affected increases, and the position of the minimum of the response moves to smaller scales as the redshift decreases. We find that lower gas fractions in groups and clusters lead to a stronger response and that the use of collimated jets instead of thermally driven winds for AGN feedback enhances the effect. Lowering the stellar masses at fixed cluster gas fractions also increases the magnitude of the response. We find only a small (1% at $k<10~h$ Mpc$^{-1}$) dependence of our results on the background cosmology, but a wider range of cosmology variations will be needed to confirm this result. The response we obtain for our strongest feedback models is compatible with some of the recent analyses combining weak lensing with external data. Such a response is, however, in strong tension with the X-ray inferred gas fractions in clusters used to calibrate the FLAMINGO model.

tool_calls.result:
arXiv ID: 2512.02954
Title: The suppression of the matter power spectrum: strong feedback from X-ray gas mass fractions, kSZ effect profiles, and galaxy-galaxy lensing
Authors: Jared Siegel, Leah Bigwood, Alexandra Amon, Jamie McCullough, Masaya Yamamoto, Ian G. McCarthy, Matthieu Schaller, Aurel Schneider, Joop Schaye
Year: 2025
Abstract: Baryon feedback redistributes gas relative to the underlying dark matter distribution and suppresses the matter power spectrum on small scales, but the amplitude and scale dependence of this effect are uncertain. We constrain the impact of baryon feedback on the matter power spectrum by jointly analysing X-ray gas mass fractions from the eROSITA and HSC-XXL samples and SDSS/DESI+ACT kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect profiles; the samples are characterised with galaxy-galaxy lensing and together span group and cluster masses at $0<z<1$. Using the baryonification framework, our joint eROSITA and kSZ model gives precise constraints on the suppression of the matter power spectrum: $10 \pm 2\%$ at $k=1~h~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. The inferred gas profiles are more extended and the power suppression is stronger than predicted by the fiducial models of recent hydrodynamical simulation suites, including FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS. The HSC-XXL gas mass fractions, which the fiducial simulations were calibrated to reproduce, prefer more moderate power suppression than the kSZ and eROSITA data: $5 \pm 4\%$ at $k=1~h~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. With a simulated LSST Year 1 weak lensing analysis, we demonstrate a framework for next-generation surveys: calibrating feedback models with multi-wavelength gas observables to recover the small-scale statistical power of cosmic shear.

Title: A non-linear solution to the $S_8$ tension?
Authors: Alexandra Amon, George Efstathiou
Year: 2022

A non-linear solution to the S8 tension?
Alexandra Amon 1⋆, George Efstathiou 1†
1 Kavli Institute for Cosmology Cambridge, Madingley Road, Cambridge, CB3 OHA.
24 June 2022
ABSTRACT
Weak galaxy lensing surveys have consistently reported a lower amplitude for the
matter ﬂuctuation spectrum, as measured by the S8 parameter, than expected in the
ΛCDM cosmology favoured by Planck. However, the expansion history follows the
predictions of the Planck ΛCDM cosmology to high accuracy, as do measurements of
lensing of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies. Redshift space distortion
measurements also appear to be consistent with Planck ΛCDM. In this paper, we
argue that these observations can be reconciled with the Planck ΛCDM cosmology
if the matter power spectrum is suppressed more strongly on non-linear scales than
assumed in analyses of weak galaxy lensing. We demonstrate this point by ﬁtting a
one-parameter model, characterising a suppression of the non-linear power spectrum,
to the KiDS-1000 weak lensing measurements. Such a suppression could be attributed
to new properties of the dark matter that aﬀect non-linear scales, or to a response of
the matter ﬂuctuations to baryonic feedback processes that are stronger than expected
from recent cosmological simulations. Our proposed explanation can be tested using
measurements of the amplitude of the matter ﬂuctuation spectrum on linear scales, in
particular via high precision redshift space distortion measurements from forthcoming
galaxy and quasar redshift surveys.
Key words: cosmology: cosmological parameters, weak lensing, observations

A detailed analysis of the two-point correlation func-
tions ξ±, as measured by KiDS21, shows that the Planck
ΛCDM model can provide acceptable ﬁts if the power-
spectrum on non-linear scales is suppressed via our phe-
nomenological model of Eq. 4, with a value Amod ≈ 0.69.
If this suppression is interpreted as being caused by bary-
onic feedback, then a comparison with numerical hydrody-
namic simulations shows that strong baryonic feedback is
required. The amplitude and spatial extent of the suppres-
sion that we require are well outside the ranges found in the
BAHAMAS simulations and cannot be reproduced by bary-
onic feedback models adopted in KiDS21 and Tr¨ oster et al.
(2021) given their choices of priors. However, the physics of
baryonic feedback is extremely complex and multi-scale and
it may be premature to exclude models with strong baryonic
feedback. As mentioned in Sect. 3.3, combinations of cosmic
shear with thermal and kinetic SZ measurements provide
hints that baryonic feedback may be stronger than conven-
tionally thought (Amodeo et al. 2021; Schneider et al. 2021;
Tr¨ oster et al. 2022). In particular, kinetic SZ measurements
oﬀer the possibility of constraining the eﬀects of baryonic
feedback into the mildly non-linear regime.
Recently some evidence for low values of S8, though
not at high statistical signiﬁcance, has come from cross-
correlations of CMB lensing with photometric galaxy cat-
alogues (Marques et al. 2020; Robertson et al. 2021; Hang
et al. 2021; Krolewski et al. 2021; Chang et al. 2022; White
et al. 2022), or with galaxy redshift surveys (Chen et al.
2022a). In some of these analyses, modiﬁcations to the non-
linear power spectrum as proposed in this paper may in-
crease the inferred values of S8. For others (e.g. Chen et al.
2022a) the low values of S8 are driven by cross-correlations
at large angular scales that are insensitive to the non-linear
power spectrum but may be aﬀected by selection biases. An
analysis of galaxy-lensing cross-correlations shows that the
preference for low values ofS8 comes from measurements at
small scales (Amon et al. 2022a).
It is important to recognise the possibility that a sup-
pression of the matter power spectrum on non-linear scales
may be a consequence of new physics in the dark sector. For
example, a suppression would arise if a fraction of the dark
matter were in the form of a light axionic particle with a de
Broglie wavelength of a few Mpc (Widrow & Kaiser 1993; Hu
et al. 2000; Hui et al. 2017) though there are many other pos-
sibilities as discussed by Hooper et al. (2022). More detailed
investigations of such models would be worthwhile, partic-
ularly if it can be demonstrated deﬁnitively that baryonic
feedback cannot solve the S8 tension. In the longer term, it
may be possible to diﬀerentiate between baryonic feedback
and the physics of dark matter by measuring the redshift
dependence of the matter power spectrum suppression (Viel
et al. 2013) and using the high redshift reach of the quasar
Lyman-α forest as discussed by Hooper et al. (2022).

ABSTRACT
Weak galaxy lensing surveys have consistently reported a lower amplitude for the
matter ﬂuctuation spectrum, as measured by the S8 parameter, than expected in the
ΛCDM cosmology favoured by Planck. However, the expansion history follows the
predictions of the Planck ΛCDM cosmology to high accuracy, as do measurements of
lensing of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies. Redshift space distortion
measurements also appear to be consistent with Planck ΛCDM. In this paper, we
argue that these observations can be reconciled with the Planck ΛCDM cosmology
if the matter power spectrum is suppressed more strongly on non-linear scales than
assumed in analyses of weak galaxy lensing. We demonstrate this point by ﬁtting a
one-parameter model, characterising a suppression of the non-linear power spectrum,
to the KiDS-1000 weak lensing measurements. Such a suppression could be attributed
to new properties of the dark matter that aﬀect non-linear scales, or to a response of
the matter ﬂuctuations to baryonic feedback processes that are stronger than expected
from recent cosmological simulations. Our proposed explanation can be tested using
measurements of the amplitude of the matter ﬂuctuation spectrum on linear scales, in
particular via high precision redshift space distortion measurements from forthcoming
galaxy and quasar redshift surveys.

ABSTRACT
The effect of baryon physics associated with galaxy formation onto the large-scale matter distribution of the Universe is a key
uncertainty in the theoretical modelling required for the interpretation of Stage IV cosmology surveys. We use the F LAMINGO
suite of simulations to study the baryon response due to galaxy formation of the total matter power spectrum. We find that it
is only well converged for simulation volumes in excess of 2003 Mpc3. We report results for simulations of varying feedback
intensity, which either match the X-ray inferred gas fractions in clusters and the z = 0 stellar mass function, or shifted versions
of the data, as well as for different implementations of AGN feedback. We package our results in the form of a Gaussian process
emulator which can rapidly reproduce all the simulations’ predictions to better than one per cent up to the comoving wavenumber
k = 10 h· Mpc−1 and up to z = 3 for all the feedback models present in the FLAMINGO suite. We find that the response becomes
stronger, the range of scales affected increases, and the position of the minimum of the response moves to smaller scales as

3.2 Verification and accuracy
Before exploring the results, we start by assessing the quality of the
emulator’s predictions for the data points it was trained on.
In Fig. 2, we show the baryon response for our fiducial model
(fgas+0σ, M∗ + 0σ, jet 0%) at 21 different redshifts and for 61 dif-
ferent values of k. Recall that we only trained on 7 redshifts and 31
bins in k. For each redshift, the dots indicate the raw results from the
simulation whilst the lines show the predictions of the emulator. In
the bottom panel, we present the ratio between the raw simulation
results and the emulator predictions, with the grey shaded regions
indicating 0.5 and 1 per cent differences respectively.
Before discussing the performance of the emulator, we analyse
the evolution with redshift of the response. We find that the re-
sponse becomes stronger as the simulation evolves. The position of
the minimum of the response moves from k = 6 h· Mpc−1 at z = 2 to
k = 10 h·Mpc−1 at z = 0. The range of scales affected by baryons also
increases with decreasing redshift. At z = 2, the response is negligi-
ble up to scales k≈ 1 h· Mpc−1, with the departure from unity (i.e.
no response) shifting to k≈ 0.1 h· Mpc−1 by z = 0.
Turning now to the verification of our model, we find that for all
redshifts shown and for all k< 10 h· Mpc−1, the emulator described
above can reproduce the simulation data with an accuracy better than

accurate but still returns an answer with a relative error better than2
per cent.

models it was trained on. We arbitrarily picked z = 0.5 for the
figure but verified that the results are identical at other redshifts.

the emulator reaches a relative accuracy better than 1 per cent for

matter power spectrum required to resolve theS8 tension between DES and thePlanck
ΛCDM model is not as strong as inferred using KiDS data, but is still more extreme
than predictions from recent numerical simulations. An alternative possibility is that
non-standard dark matter contributes to the required suppression. We investigate the
redshift and scale dependence of the suppression of the matter power spectrum. If
our proposed explanation of the S8 tension is correct, the required suppression must
extend into the mildly non-linear regime to wavenumbersk∼ 0.2hMpc−1. In addition,
all measures of S8 using linear scales should agree with the Planck ΛCDM cosmology,
an expectation that will be testable to high precision in the near future.

as recent measurements from Advanced ACT are consis-
tent with the Planck cosmology (Madhavacheril et al. 2023).
Cross-correlations of CMB lensing with galaxy surveys can
provide an important test of this hypothesis. Forthcoming
analyses using the latest CMB lensing maps from ACT (Qu
et al. 2023) and the South Pole Telescope (Omori et al.
2023) should agree with the predictions of thePlanck ΛCDM
model.
As reviewed in Paper I redshift-space distortions mea-
sured from linear scales from current galaxy redshift surveys
are consistent with our interpretation, but not to high pre-
cision. This situation should change decisively in the near
future with RSD measurements from DESI (see e.g. Schlegel
et al. 2022, and references therein). Measurements ofS8 from
quasar Ly-alpha lines from DESI uniquely give access to
high k and z >
∼ 1 and oﬀer an opportunity to potentially
break the degeneracy between baryonic feedback and non-
standard dark matter. Tests of a redshift-dependent growth,
σ8(z) or S8(z) using measurements from from linear scales
should be consistent with ΛCDM (White et al. 2022; DES
Collaboration et al. 2022; Garc´ ıa-Garc´ ıa et al. 2021)8.
Weak galaxy lensing measurements oﬀer a window to
a wide range of scales as indicated in Fig. 8. In the future,
it may be possible to reconstruct the power spectrum as
a function of wavenumber and redshift from weak lensing
data. Assuming that systematic errors can be suﬃciently
mitigated, it may become possible to accurately test the
ΛCDM cosmology on linear scales and to reconstruct the
matter power spectrum on small scales using weak galaxy
lensing data alone. Such an analysis would establish unam-
biguously whether the S8 tension is caused by a deviation
from the ΛCDM model at late times, or whether it is an
apparent tension caused by physics on non-linear scales.

stellar fraction in their haloes and this likely explains part of the dif-

match SP(k) more closely. One could, for instance, lower “M∗± Nσ”
whilst increasing “fgas±Nσ” in order to maintain the same baryon
fraction in haloes. However, as we do not have predictions for the
stellar fractions as a function of these parameters, we leave this ex-
ercise for a future study with a more comprehensive emulator. This
simple comparison nevertheless indicates that predicting the bary-
onic response using a single number (e.g. the baryon or gas fraction)
per halo mass bin may not be sufficient and more complex models
will have to be constructed in the future.
4.4.3 Can FLAMINGO feedback solve the S 8 tension?
Over the last few years, precision tests of the ΛCDM mod-
els, particularly those exploiting low-redshift weak-lensing and
large-scale structure probes, have reported measurements of S 8≡
σ8
√Ωm/0.3 in conflict with the value inferred from the primary
CMB anisotropies and BAO experiments. Depending on the data
sets and their analysis, this so-called tension can reach 3σ (Hey-
mans et al. 2021; Abbott et al. 2022; Amon et al. 2023; Miyatake
et al. 2023; McCarthy et al. 2023; Terasawa et al. 2025).
Among the different solutions put forward to solve this tension,
the possibility that (baryon and galactic feedback) physics on the
scales of groups and clusters contributes to the non-linear effects on
the range of scales on which the power spectrum is probed is an in-
teresting proposition as it does not require an alteration of the back-
ground cosmological model. We explore here whether the response
obtained in the F LAMINGO model is compatible with the required
baryon-induced non-linear solution to the tension.
Amon & Efstathiou (2022) constructed a toy model for the ef-
fect of baryons, inspired by the functional form obtained from the
HMC ODE 2020 (Mead et al. 2020), and constrained it to reconcile
the weak-lensing shear analysis of the KiDS-1000 survey and the
primary CMB anisotropy data. Using a similar approach, Preston
et al. (2023) combined the DES year 3 shear data to the CMB data
to also constrain the required non-linear power spectrum changes.
Both these constraints are shown as, respectively, the blue and ma-
genta shaded regions in the right panel of Fig. 13 (see also Ferreira
et al. 2024, for an analysis combining DES lensing to ROSAT X-ray
all-sky photon counts). A parallel approach is to exploit the weak-
lensing data alone in combination with a halo model or emulator for
the baryonic response. The analysis of Aricò et al. (2023) and Big-
wood et al. (2024), both exploiting the DES year 3 data but with
different emulators — BACCO (Aricò et al. 2021), BC EMU (Giri
& Schneider 2021), respectively — and different analysis pipelines,
are shown as shaded regions in the left panel of Fig. 13 alongside the
results of García-García et al. (2024) also using the BACCO emu-
lator but combining data from DES, KiDS and HSC. The results of
Terasawa et al. (2025) exploiting HSC data and the HM CODE 2020
halo model are also shown. Finally, additional datasets informing the
emulators or models on the gaseous content of haloes can be used.
The constraints of Bigwood et al. (2024) including kSZ data from
ACT are shown in the right panel of Fig. 13 (see also Schneider
et al. 2022). In both panels, we show the response obtained for four
models spanning the range of FLAMINGO emulator input parameter
values.
As can be seen, the more extreme models in the F LAMINGO
suite are compatible with some of the inferred baryonic responses in
these studies. In particular, both “fgas−8σ” models (i.e. with ther-

added kSZ constraints). Interestingly, these FLAMINGO models dis-

args.claim: Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) find that to reconcile DES Y3 cosmic shear with Planck LCDM, the non-linear suppression needed is weaker than the KiDS-1000 value (A_mod ~ 0.69). It is still more extreme than recent hydrodynamic simulations predict, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. The DES Y3 A_mod value itself was not in the text I read (abstract and conclusions), so it remains unsourced.
args.note: Abstract quote: 'The non-linear suppression of the matter power spectrum required to resolve the S8 tension between DES and the Planck LCDM model is not as strong as inferred using KiDS data, but is still more extreme than predictions from recent numerical simulations.' Model: P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL - P_L). The numerical DES A_mod lies in the body text between chars 6000 and 48000, which I did not read. Not run through cite (budget).

args.claim: Second mitigation method (Maraio, Hall & Taylor, 2410.12500): a theoretical-error covariance built into the matter power spectrum, used in place of binary ell scale cuts. For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models can introduce significant bias. The theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in variance, and it removes the need to choose an ell_max for each bin. This places the baryon-sensitive shear range up to ell ~ 5000.
args.note: Abstract quote: 'our theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels, with only a modest increase in parameter variances.' The first mitigation method, multi-wavelength calibration from 2512.02954, is already in f-004. Neither paper was run through cite (budget).

args.claim: Approximate comparison only. The HACC emulator gives about 0.8-0.9% suppression at k=0.5 h/Mpc, about 0.03-0.04% at k=0.1 h/Mpc and at most 2.5% at k=1 h/Mpc (f-001, f-002). This is far below the A_mod-type suppression that Amon-Efstathiou and Preston et al. require. That suppression scales the whole non-linear part of P(k) (A_mod ~ 0.69 for KiDS, weaker but still beyond simulations for DES) and reaches down to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Within its design range, the emulator cannot approach the suppression needed to reconcile shear with Planck. A projected C_ell or xi_+ forecast is future work, since no tool computes it.

args.claim: FLAMINGO (2410.17109, quoted and cited as arxiv241017109). For the fiducial model, the minimum of P/P_DMO moves from k=6 h/Mpc at z=2 to k=10 h/Mpc at z=0. The departure from unity begins at k~1 h/Mpc at z=2 and at k~0.1 h/Mpc at z=0. At z=0, across thermal-AGN fgas variants from -10 sigma to +4 sigma, the minimum stays at k=8-10 h/Mpc. The fgas parameter mainly changes the normalisation of the response, and the response saturates below fgas-8 sigma (an emulator extrapolation). The jet model has a stronger response at negative fgas but a similar k-range and minimum position. The text gives no numerical depth for the z=0 minimum: it appears only in Figs. 2, 5 and 6 of the paper, whose y-axes run from 0.75 to 1.10. Both fgas-8sigma models (thermal and jet) fall inside the ranges of Bigwood et al. 2024, with or without kSZ. The Amon & Efstathiou 2022 response is out of reach of the FLAMINGO emulator.

args.claim:
One-at-a-time sensitivity of HACC Pk-ratio at z=0. Except for the parameter varied, all runs use the fiducial point (e_w=0.6, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61, M_seed=1.3, kappa_w=3, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8).
Suppression, 1-P_hydro/P_grav (emulator 1-sigma in brackets):
- kappa_w=2: 2.92% (0.15%) at k=0.997; 10.93% (0.54%) at k=3.007; 13.66% (0.64%) at k=3.714 h/Mpc.
- kappa_w=4: 1.31% (0.13%) at k=0.997; 4.95% (0.46%) at k=3.007; 6.60% (0.54%) at k=3.714 h/Mpc.
- M_seed=2.0: 2.42% (0.14%) at k=0.997; 9.03% (0.49%) at k=3.007; 11.40% (0.57%) at k=3.714 h/Mpc.
- Fiducial, from f-001: 2.17% (0.10%) at k=0.997, 8.03% (0.35%) at k=3.01, 10.2% at k=3.71 h/Mpc.
Lower kappa_w therefore strengthens suppression.
Ranking by shift from fiducial:
- At k=1: lowering e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their lower bounds (-2.4 pp, d-01 weak point) > kappa_w over 2 to 4 (1.6 pp spread; +0.75 pp at kappa_w=2, -0.86 pp at kappa_w=4) > raising e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together to their upper bounds (+0.33 pp) > M_seed 1.3 to 2.0 (+0.25 pp).
- At k=3: the joint lowering (about -8.8 pp) > kappa_w (5.98 pp spread; +2.9 pp at kappa_w=2) > M_seed (+1.0 pp) > the joint raising (+0.76 pp).
At k=3 every one of these shifts exceeds the emulator 1-sigma of 0.35-0.54%. At k=1 the M_seed shift and the joint-raising shift are only about 2 sigma.

args.claim:
Restatement of f-002, restricted to the sampled points only. Six in-range points have been sampled: fiducial, strong, weak, kappa_w=2, kappa_w=4 and M_seed=2.
At k=1 h/Mpc and z=0, their suppression ranges from -0.2% to 2.9%; the maximum is 2.92+/-0.15% at kappa_w=2. None reaches 5% or 10%. The most suppressed point:
- is consistent with HSC-XXL (5+/-4%) within about 0.5 sigma;
- falls short of eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2%, 2512.02954) by about 3.5 sigma.
At k=3 h/Mpc the largest sampled suppression is 10.9+/-0.5% (kappa_w=2). This is below the 18.4 (+2.6/-3.1)% from 2309.02920 by about 2.4 sigma, using the lower observational error.
This is a check of the sampled models only. Combined extremes, for example kappa_w=2 together with high e_w, v_kin, eps_kin and M_seed, were not sampled, and no claim is made about the full design range.

args.why: read_text_file has no offset parameter and truncates each 799-bin CSV near k=3.73 h/Mpc. In all of the new runs (kappa_w=2, kappa_w=4, M_seed=2) the suppression is still deepening monotonically at that k. The minimum and any high-k upturn therefore remain unresolved above k=3.73 h/Mpc. A header-free copy for load_table_data would need a file-writing tool, which is not available. The comparison plot was not made because the budget ran out.
